name: Park Hyatt Istanbul – Macka Palas
positioning: Park Hyatt hotel in the 1922 Art Deco Maçka Palas building, originally a private residence, in Istanbul's Nişantaşı neighborhood
best_for: Travelers who want a Nişantaşı base with boutiques, restaurants and galleries steps away
Guests who want a suite with a private Turkish hammam
Diners who want several restaurants in the building, from Cipriani to Nusr-Et

facts.text: The Art Deco Maçka Palas building was conceived as a private residence.
Condé Nast Traveler notes the hotel integrates two buildings and takes its name from the older wing.
The hotel's spaces feature curated works of art, including photography by Ara Güler.
The hotel is in Nişantaşı, where boutiques, restaurants and galleries are steps away.
Dolmabahçe Palace, the Bosphorus waterfront and Maçka Park are within minutes of the hotel.
Rooms have French balconies with views across the Nişantaşı rooftops and, in select suites, towards the Bosphorus.
The Palazzo Suite includes a billiards table.
Cipriani Istanbul has mahogany walls, marble floors and the Cipriani aquarium.
Nusr-Et Maçka Palas is a steakhouse within the hotel.
Kapicciiiinoo, Nusret Gökçe's first coffee concept, is located within the hotel.
Kalimera Istanbul serves Aegean cuisine with fresh seafood, traditional mezedes and handmade Greek desserts.
The Spa offers Turkish hammam rituals.

highlights.text: The Maçka Palas building was designed by Giulio Mongeri and completed in 1922.
Select suites feature a private Turkish hammam, a steam room and Dornbracht rainfall showers.
The Lobby Lounge serves loose-leaf teas, sweet and savory bites and cocktails with live harp and cello music each afternoon.
Cipriani Istanbul is within the hotel and serves Venetian cuisine, including Carpaccio, Bellinis and Pappardelle Cipriani.
Roof Bar 805 is an open-air bar on the eighth floor with views towards the Bosphorus.

considerations.text: The taxi ride from Istanbul Airport takes about 40-60 minutes depending on traffic.
The M2 metro line is a 10-minute walk from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
